issues.title: Bundle: per-value BitPacking select for sparse filtered scans + exact BF up to 2^27 bits at 1024 bits/key
issues.hypothesis: (1) In filtered table scans, the non-filter columns are fully decoded even when few rows pass. BitPacking has no `select` callback, so StandardColumnData::Select (standard_column_data.cpp:103) falls back to ColumnData::Select: Scan the whole vector, then result.Slice. Measured hot on lineitem, where every column involved is BitPacking (pragma_storage_info): `max()` over 5 extra columns WHERE l_partkey<100000 (5% pass) takes 88-95ms, and WHERE l_partkey<10000 (0.5% pass) takes 94-95ms. The same filter with count(*) takes 26-28ms. So the ~65ms spent fetching the extra columns does not depend on selectivity at all. A prior-run attempt (auto-memory bitpacking-select-no-gain) decoded only the selected 32-value blocks. At 5% selectivity about 80% of blocks still hold a selected row (1-0.95^32), so it saved almost nothing and got 0%. That was a bad implementation of a good idea. Reading each selected value straight from the bitstream makes the cost scale with sel_count. q09's lineitem scan (60M rows -> 3.27M, 5 extra columns l_suppkey/l_orderkey/l_extendedprice/l_discount/l_quantity) and q05's lineitem scan (60M -> 2.03M, 3 extra columns) are exactly this case. (2) Re-land the E0025 tier, retired twice as a near-miss: q05 -9/-18/-20% and -13.5/-17.9/-17.4% against a -20.3% bar, with no regressions. Adding (1) on q05's own lineitem scan should push q05 past the bar.
issues.plan: Part 1, src/storage/compression/bitpacking.cpp: add `template <class T> void BitpackingSelect(ColumnSegment &segment, ColumnScanState &state, idx_t vector_count, Vector &result, const SelectionVector &sel, idx_t sel_count)` and register it in GetBitpackingFunction (line ~964) through the CompressionFunction constructor's select slot. Count the nullptr args against rle.cpp:592 / numeric_constant.cpp:221, which pass the select function in that position. Select contract: the result is FLAT and holds the sel_count selected values compacted (result_data[i] = value at sel.get_index(i)), and the scan state advances by vector_count. sel is ascending, as RLESelect assumes. Implementation: use BitpackingScanState (line 608) and walk metadata groups exactly as BitpackingScanPartial (line 775) does. When current_group_offset reaches BITPACKING_METADATA_GROUP_SIZE, call LoadNextGroup. Handle each mode within one metadata group as follows. CONSTANT: write the constant. CONSTANT_DELTA: frame_of_reference + delta*offset, copied from ScanPartial. FOR: per-value extraction, for T of 4 or 8 bytes only. The fastpforlib layout (third_party/fastpforlib/bitpacking.cpp Unroller, 32-bit words, LSB-first) makes each 32-value algorithm group a little-endian bitstream: value j sits at bit j*width from the block start, block start = current_group_ptr + (offset - offset%32)*width/8. Read ceil((bitoff%8 + width)/8) bytes with memcpy so nothing is read past the end, shift, mask, then add current_frame_of_reference with the same unsigned wrapping as the scan path. If width > 56 or T is 1/2/16 bytes, use the existing block unpack instead. DELTA_FOR (needs a prefix sum), or sel_count > vector_count/4: decode with the existing ScanPartial logic into a thread-local scratch buffer, then gather. Finally advance the state by the rows consumed, using the same bookkeeping as Skip/ScanPartial. Verify validity: for NOT NULL columns the validity is Constant, which already has select (numeric_constant.cpp ConstantSelect); ValiditySelect covers the uncompressed case. Correctness: in a debug or temporary check, compare against a full scan. Test via `dbe-tool sql` with TEMP tables of INT/BIGINT/DECIMAL columns containing NULLs, sorted data (DELTA_FOR), constant runs, widths 1..63, and selective filters at 0.1%, 5%, 30% and 90%. Compare with `SET disabled_optimizers` / filters written as `col+0` so the filter is not pushed. Part 2, src/execution/operator/join/physical_hash_join.cpp TrySetExactBloomFilter: add the exact-bitmap tier range < min(2^27, count*1024). Cap the multiplication at 2^27 for EVERY build size, not only count <= 2^17 (E0026 lesson). Keep the 128 bits/key rule, the 2^22 floor and the 2^32 guard. Measure with the warm JSON profile: lineitem scan CPU in q05 and q09 before/after.
issues.expected_gain: Micro: 5-col selective lineitem fetch 95ms -> ~40ms. q09 -5..-8% (5 extra cols at 5.4% pass), q05 -20..-25% (E0025 -17% plus select), q17/q19/q14 a few % (selective lineitem scans via BF or date filters). Geomean about -3..-4%.
issues.generality: Every filtered scan over BitPacking (the default integer/decimal compression) where the filters or join BFs pass under ~25% of rows: TPC-H q06/q12/q14/q15/q17/q19/q20-style scans, star-schema fact scans with BF. Dense filters (>25% pass) keep the current decode path through the threshold, so they should not slow down. DELTA_FOR columns (sorted keys) get no benefit. Part 2 only changes the BF representation for builds with range < 2^27.
issues.risk: Medium. Bit-level extraction must exactly match fastunpack layout and FOR wrap arithmetic; mitigated by restricting to 4/8-byte T with width<=56 and falling back otherwise, plus a randomized sql comparison. The scan state must advance correctly across metadata-group boundaries (mirror ScanPartial). Part 2 has passed hidden validation twice.

## Memory (gen2)

## State
- gen1 (r1-r16): accepted E0001 JoinDependent rule order (q19), E0002 contains() selectivity (q09), E0003 perfect HJ RIGHT (q13), E0005 BF first key multi-key HJ (q09), E0006 key-set range filter through compress projs (q18), E0007 exact bitmap BF, E0011 semi-join estimate, E0012 OR-of-ranges mask, E0014 FSST simple decode + substring prefilter (q13), E0016 DELIM_GET-build BF (q22 -20%). Best 1.281x.
- gen2 r1+r2: E0017/E0018 (no CM on hash-join keys) RETIRED twice: hidden validation regressed. DEAD.
- gen2 r5: E0021 = bundle of E0019 (deliminate SEMI) + E0020 (exact BF through CM offset) ACCEPTED. Each had been retired alone in r3/r4.
- gen2 r6: E0022 exact-BF small-range floor ACCEPTED (geomean -9.9%).
- gen2 r7: E0023 ANTI deliminator ACCEPTED (q22 -22..-29%).
- gen2 r8: E0024 parallel perfect-HJ build + INNER dense <=4M ACCEPTED (q14 -7%). Best 1.524x.
- gen2 r9: E0025 exact BF up to 2^27 at 1024 bits/key RETIRED (q05 -9/-18/-20%, bar -20.3%).
- gen2 r10: E0026 = fused hashed BF probe + E0025 RETIRED (q05 -13.5/-17.9/-17.4%, geomean -1.8%). The fused probe gave no visible gain: no visible BF stays hashed once exact tiers apply.
- gen2 r11: DISPATCHED a bundle: per-value BitPacking select + the E0025 tier (fused probe dropped).
- Claude auto-memory (~/.claude/.../memory) holds results from a PREVIOUS evolve run on this codebase. Treat them as strong measured priors, not landed code.
- .dbe/issues.md backlog: all 5 entries are stale or dead. Nothing useful there.

## Acceptance lessons
- Acceptance needs BOTH: some template faster beyond its noise AND a visible geomean that improves. Any template slower beyond its noise also gets an issue retired.
- Bundle a near-miss (like E0025) with a general second mechanism that hits the SAME template (q05 here).

## Key finding r11: BitPacking non-filter columns are fully decoded regardless of selectivity
- Hot micro test: `max()` over 5 lineitem columns WHERE l_partkey<100000 (5%) = 88-95ms; WHERE l_partkey<10000 (0.5%) = 95ms; count(*) with the same filter = 27ms. All lineitem columns are BitPacking.
- Cause: bitpacking.cpp registers no `select`, so StandardColumnData::Select (standard_column_data.cpp:103) falls back to Scan + Slice. Fetch path: row_group.cpp:809-819. Only RLE, Constant, FSST, dict_fsst, uncompressed string and validity have select.
- The prior-run "bitpacking select no gain" used 32-block decode. At 5% selectivity, 80% of blocks hold a selected row, so it saved nothing. Per-value bit extraction is the fix (fastpforlib layout = LSB-first little-endian bitstream per 32-value group for 32/64-bit T). DELTA_FOR cannot do random access.
- If r11 fails: check whether per-value select was actually reached (FOR mode vs DELTA_FOR on these columns), and measure the micro test before/after.

## Key finding r9: an exact bitmap BF probe is ~2x cheaper than a hashed BF probe
- q05 lineitem scan 0.92s -> 0.48s CPU with an exact BF. Hashed path = slice + Hash + Flatten + LookupHashes.

## Key finding r8: perfect HJ build was serial (fixed in E0024)
- Follow-ups: q13 RIGHT perfect join found-match flush is still serial (small).
- How to A/B a threshold without code changes: add a key-range or date predicate just under/over the limit.

## Large perfect HA (E0009/E0013): q13 -20% real but q18 +8% beyond noise each time
- Possible cause: 22-bit per-thread tables (~64MB each x 8) leave the allocator/page-fault state bad for q18. A retry needs range-sized tables or buffer-pool memory. Unverified.

## Measured
- q09 (cold JSON r11): lineitem scan 3.8s CPU (60M->3.27M, BF on l_partkey exact, 5 extra cols); HJ o_orderkey=l_orderkey 1.42s CPU (build 3.27M lineitem-side, probe orders 2.94M after exact BF); HJ l_partkey,l_suppkey 0.65s; agg 0.21s.
- q13: inner agg 1.95s CPU (15.3M rows, 1.5M groups, 127ns/row), orders scan 1.66s (NOT LIKE), decompress proj 0.23s, RIGHT HJ 0.25s.
- q05: lineitem scan 0.93s, HJ l_orderkey 0.38s (455k build, 2M probe), multi-key HJ (c_nationkey,s_nationkey + suppkey) 0.15s, 1.82M->72k rows.
- q13 eager aggregation as a manual rewrite: only -4%. DEAD.
- HJ build ~126ns/row on 7.2M orders. HJ prefetch: no gain. The HT already uses salts.
- dbe-tool profile output looks COLD. Use the warm JSON trick.
- No PK/UNIQUE constraints in the schema.

## How to get full operator timings
- dbe-tool sql "<warm q>; <warm q>; SET enable_profiling='json'; SET profiling_output='/home/shresth/dev/db_evolve/work/slots/slot0/.dbe/scratch_x.json'; <q>" then Grep '"operator_timing"|"operator_name"|"operator_cardinality"|Dynamic Filters'. /tmp is NOT readable.
- Micro A/B: repeat a statement 3x in one dbe-tool sql call and read the last timings (the first run is ~3-5x slower).

## Key finding: CM on join keys blocks the BF
- physical_hash_join.cpp FinalizeFilters: BF only if !has_cast && no storage_offset, except an exact BF through the offset on cond 0 (E0021).
- Exact BF: TrySetExactBloomFilter caps EXACT_BF_MAX_BITS_PER_KEY=128, EXACT_BF_SMALL_RANGE=1<<22, MAX_RANGE=1<<32. Hashed BF: 12 bits/key.
- PushRangeSetFilter (gap-split ranges) only for 50 < keys <= 3200.

## Measurement lessons
- Alternate A/B/A/B. Do NOT wrap in count(*) (it changes the plan); use a temp view + `from v`.
- dbe-tool bash: no pipes, no shell variables.
- Bench noise ±10-20% per template. Noise thresholds: q16 ~7.9%, q18 ~5%, q13 ~14%, q09 ~8.6%, q14 ~5.1%, q05 ~20.3%, q04 ~20%.

## Profile snapshot (r11): q18 552, q13 528, q09 460, q05 263, q08 203, q03 195, q07 194, q16 179, q04 164, q17 145, q14 138, q22 106, q19 104, q02 67. Geomean 195.2.

## Dead / exhausted
- CM join-key removal, HJ prefetch, agg run-collapse, in-place finalize, FSST heap reuse, dictionary filter, scan filter cost ordering, early HT grow, sparse perfect HJ (8M range), BF on sparse perfect HJ, hashed BF through CM offset, q13 eager aggregation, fused hashed BF probe (no visible target).
- q18: the 15M-group agg dominates (exhausted).

## Next candidates
1. (dispatched r11) the BitPacking per-value select + E0025 bundle.
2. If select works: the same for other codecs on hot paths (ALP for doubles? check storage_info on other tables).
3. q13 agg 127ns/row: a range-sized perfect HA (not 22-bit fixed), allocated so q18 is not hit.
4. q09 o_orderkey HJ 1.42s CPU: investigate build vs probe split.
5. MARK delim joins (IN/EXISTS in OR) via the deliminator: check the NULL semantics.

## Codebase facts
- CM: src/optimizer/compressed_materialization*. Rule order: src/optimizer/optimizer.cpp.
- Deliminator: src/optimizer/deliminator.cpp. Join filters: JoinFilterPushdownOptimizer::GenerateJoinFilters.
- Perfect HJ: perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp. Perfect HA: plan_aggregate.cpp. FSST: src/storage/compression/fsst.cpp. BF: src/planner/filter/bloom_filter.cpp.
- BitPacking: src/storage/compression/bitpacking.cpp (BitpackingScanState :608, ScanPartial :775, FetchRow ~:870, GetBitpackingFunction :964). Modes CONSTANT/CONSTANT_DELTA/FOR/DELTA_FOR per 2048-value metadata group.
- Budget is tight (~$4/session): read memory, the ledger tail and the profile head, then dispatch.
